title: A Phase 2b Study of CS1 Added in Participants Stable on Standard of Care Therapy for the Treatment of PAH
official: A Phase 2b, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Dose-Finding Study, to Compare the Efficacy and Safety/Tolerability of CS1 Versus Placebo When Added to Standard of Care for the Treatment of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension (PAH)
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the effect of CS1 on PVR in participants with stable PAH

interventions.name: Capsules similar to CS1 delayed release capsules

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1. Participant must be willing and able to sign a written informed consent prior to any study-related procedures and able to understand and follow instructions; return to the study unit for specified study visits; and able to participate in the study for the entire period.
2. 2. Participant is male or female, aged 18 to 80 years at the time of signing the ICF.
3. 3. Participant must have a BMI of 18 to 40 kg/m2 at screening.
4. 4. Participant with pulmonary hypertension Group 1 belonging to one of the following subgroups of Clinical Classification of PAH:  a. Idiopathic PAH  b. Heritable PAH  c. Drug or toxin-induced PAH   d. PAH associated with CTD  e. PAH associated with simple, congenital systemic-to-pulmonary shunts if at least 1 year past shunt repair.
5. 5. Participant with symptomatic PAH and reduced exercise capacity due primarily to their PAH diagnosis, having been classified by qualified individual, ie, physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner, to be in NYHA/WHO FC II or III.
6. 6. Participant with PAH having a REVEAL Lite 2 score ≥6.
7. 7. Participant receiving stable doses of SOC PAH therapies for at least 90 days prior to screening. For participants receiving sotatercept, it is not mandatory that they have been on the same dose prior to screening. However, they must have received the drug continuously for at least 180 days before screening.
8. 8. Participant has a screening hemodynamic assessment of PAH by RHC demonstrating a persistent resting mPAP ≥20 mm Hg and resting mean PVR ≥5 WU with PCWP ≤15 mmHg documented by central reading of the RHC performed during screening.
9. 9. Participant has a 6MWD ≥150 m and <550 m at screening. A maximum of 25% of enrolled participants with 6MWD of 450-550 m at screening will be included in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1. Participant with pulmonary hypertension classified as WHO Group 2, 3, 4, or 5.
2. 6. Participants with prior heart or heart-lung transplants, active on the lung transplant list, or life expectancy of <12 months. Participants who are likely to undergo lung transplantation within the next 6 months will also be excluded from the study.
3. 7. Participant has left heart failure (with signs and symptoms of heart failure) with either:  - Preserved ejection fraction defined as those with >40% ejection fraction and LAV >34 mL/m2. At the discretion of investigator, for participants with LVEF between 40% to 50%, a fluid challenge can be done to check their status.   - Reduced ejection fraction (LVEF <40%)
4. 8. Participants with more than mild mitral or aortic valve disease will be excluded. However, participants with moderate mitral regurgitation are allowed if not related to congestive heart failure.
5. 9. Participants with left ventricular regional wall motion abnormality on  ECHO at screening, suggestive of new-onset coronary artery disease within 6 months prior to the screening period. Participants with stable CAD are permitted.
6. 14. Participant has experienced a cerebrovascular accident (stroke) within 3 months prior to screening.
7. 15. Participant has any current or prior history of symptomatic coronary disease (prior myocardial infarction, percutaneous coronary intervention, coronary artery bypass graft surgery, or cardiac anginal chest pain) in the past 6 months prior to screening visit.
8. 16. Participant has acutely decompensated heart failure within 30 days prior to baseline, as per investigator assessment.
9. 17. Participant has uncontrolled hypertension defined as systolic blood pressure >160 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure >100 mmHg.
10. 18. Participant has sustained hypotension, defined as systolic blood pressure <95 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure <50 mmHg.
11. 19. Participant has sustained resting heart rate >120 beats per minute (confirmed by duplicate assessments of office vital signs) or consecutive ECG assessments on at least 3 consecutive occasions prior to or at screening.
12. 10. Participant has evidence of significant chronic thromboembolic disorder as determined by the investigator or recent pulmonary embolism within 6 months prior to screening.
13. 20. Participant has received another investigational drug within 30 days or within 5 half‑lives prior to screening or is participating in a non-interventional study which, in the opinion of the investigator, would interfere with the study compliance or outcome assessments.
14. 21. Participant is on regular treatment with sodium valproate/VPA, other anti-epilepsy drugs, or other prohibited medications that cannot be discontinued at the Screening Visit (V1).
15. 22. Participant receiving anticoagulation or antiplatelet therapy that cannot be discontinued at the Screening Visit (V1). Only a low daily dose aspirin (<125 mg) is allowed.
16. 23. Participant has a FEV1/forced vital capacity <70% (absolute), FEV1 ≤50%, or TLC <70% predicted on PFT; for potential participants with TLC 60% to 69% predicted, non-contrasted CT scan must be performed to exclude participants with more than mild interstitial lung disease. PFTs should have been obtained within 6 months prior to screening. If PFT results within 6 months prior to screening are not available then PFTs will be performed at screening.
17. 24. Participant has clinically significant renal dysfunction as defined by the eGFR of <30 mL/min/1.73m2 as calculated by the 2021 Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration equation at screening.
18. 25. Participant has significant liver dysfunction as defined by any one of the following results at screening (including participants with acute or chronic hepatitis as well as participants with own or family history of serious hepatitis, especially drug related).  a. ALT >2.0 × ULN  b. AST >2.0 × ULN  c. Serum bilirubin >1.5 × ULN  Note: Participants with bilirubin elevation with Gilbert disease can be enrolled in the  study if their direct bilirubin is within normal limits.
19. 11. Participant has a history of known pericardial constriction or restrictive or congestive cardiomyopathy.
20. 12. Participant ECG with QTcF >480 msec during the screening period.
21. 13. Participant has a personal or family history of long QTc syndrome or sudden cardiac death.
22. 2. Participant has ACHD.
23. 3. Participant has portopulmonary hypertension induced PAH.
24. 4. Participant has PAH-related schistosomiasis or history of atrial septostomy, opportunistic infection (eg, invasive candidiasis or pneumocystis pneumonia) within 6 months prior to screening; serious local infection (eg, cellulitis, abscess) or systemic infection (eg, septicemia) within 3 months prior to screening.
25. 5. Participant has concomitant medical or psychiatric disorder, condition, history, or any other condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would either put the participant at risk or impair the participant’s ability to participate in or complete the requirements of the study or confound the objectives of the study.
